Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 9 (MCQ Q5)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which protein is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere.
RuBisCO fixes $CO_2$ in the Calvin cycle. It is present in huge amounts in the chloroplasts of all green plants, so its total quantity exceeds that of any other protein.
Collagen is the tempting trap. It is the most abundant protein only in the animal world, not in the whole biosphere.
Haemoglobin and insulin are found only in certain animals and are far less abundant.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about protein structure are correct?
(i) Both right-handed and left-handed helices are commonly observed in proteins.
(ii) The entire polypeptide chain of a protein exists as a continuous helix.
(iii) Adult human haemoglobin has four subunits: two of the α type and two of the β type.
(iv) Quaternary structure is possible only in proteins made of more than one polypeptide or subunit.
(v) Tertiary structure gives a three-dimensional view of a protein and is absolutely necessary for many of its biological activities.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: only right-handed helices are observed in proteins.
(ii) Incorrect: only some portions of the thread form a helix. Other regions fold in different ways.
(iii) Correct: adult human haemoglobin has 4 subunits, two α and two β.
(iv) Correct: quaternary structure needs more than one polypeptide or subunit.
(v) Correct: tertiary structure gives the 3-D shape and is absolutely necessary for many biological activities.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (enzyme class) with List-II (type of reaction catalysed):
List-I
A. Transferases
B. Hydrolases
C. Lyases
D. Ligases
List-II
I. Hydrolysis of peptide or glycosidic bonds
II. Transfer of a group other than hydrogen between two substrates
III. Joining of two compounds by forming C–O, C–S or C–N bonds
IV. Removal of groups by a mechanism other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation:
A. Transferases move a group other than hydrogen from one substrate to another, so A-II.
B. Hydrolases break ester, ether, peptide and glycosidic bonds by adding water, so B-I.
C. Lyases remove groups without hydrolysis and leave double bonds, so C-IV.
D. Ligases join two compounds by forming C–O, C–S, C–N or P–O bonds, so D-III.
Option (1) is a trap because it swaps lyases and ligases.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A tissue homogenised in trichloroacetic acid was filtered, and the acid-insoluble fraction (retentate) was analysed. How many of the following would be expected in the retentate?
Glucose, Proteins, Amino acids, Nucleic acids, Polysaccharides, Nucleotides, Lipids, Inorganic phosphate
questions.explanation:
The acid-insoluble retentate contains only four kinds of organic compounds.
In the retentate: proteins, nucleic acids and polysaccharides (all polymers), plus lipids, which come along as insoluble membrane vesicles.
In the acid-soluble filtrate: glucose, amino acids, nucleotides and inorganic phosphate, because they are small molecules.
Total in the retentate = 4. Students often forget to count lipids.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Inorganic compounds like sulphate and phosphate are detected in the acid-soluble fraction of a living tissue.
Reason (R): The acid-soluble fraction contains only organic compounds.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that inorganic compounds such as sulphate and phosphate are detected in the acid-soluble fraction.
R is false. The acid-soluble pool contains organic small molecules (sugars, amino acids, nucleotides) as well as inorganic ions and compounds. It does not contain only organic compounds.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following nitrogenous bases is a substituted purine?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: adenine and guanine are substituted purines. Cytosine, uracil and thymine are substituted pyrimidines.
Guanine is therefore the purine among the options.
Thymine may tempt because it is a DNA base, but it is a pyrimidine.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are made mainly of cellulose?
Cotton fibre; paper made from plant pulp; plant cell wall; exoskeleton of a cockroach; glycogen granules in liver cells
questions.explanation:
Cotton fibre: cellulose ✔
Paper from plant pulp: cellulose ✔
Plant cell wall: cellulose ✔
Cockroach exoskeleton: chitin ✘
Liver granules: glycogen ✘
So 3 items are made mainly of cellulose.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Malonate
(b) Haem
(c) Zinc
(d) Niacin
List-II
(i) Prosthetic group of catalase
(ii) Cofactor of carboxypeptidase
(iii) Vitamin component of NAD
(iv) Competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase
questions.explanation:
(a) Malonate closely resembles succinate, so it competitively inhibits succinic dehydrogenase. This gives (a)-(iv).
(b) Haem is the prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase. This gives (b)-(i).
(c) Zinc is the metal-ion cofactor of carboxypeptidase. This gives (c)-(ii).
(d) Niacin is the vitamin present in the coenzymes NAD and NADP. This gives (d)-(iii).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When we homogenise any tissue in an acid the acid soluble pool represents
questions.explanation:
Grinding tissue in acid separates it into two fractions.
The acid-insoluble fraction holds macromolecules: proteins, nucleic acids and polysaccharides. Lipids also end up here because membranes break into vesicles.
The acid-soluble pool holds small molecules such as amino acids, sugars and nucleotides.
According to NCERT, this soluble pool roughly represents the cytoplasmic composition. Membranes, the nucleus and mitochondria are structures made of macromolecules, so they do not fit.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 9 (MCQ Q7)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A person follows a diet that completely lacks protein for a long period. Based on the role of dietary proteins, which amino acids are most likely to become deficient in the body?
options: Essential amino acids, because the body cannot make them and must obtain them from food
Non-essential amino acids, because they can be obtained only from dietary proteins
All 20 amino acids equally, because the body cannot make any amino acid
None, because the body can synthesise all amino acids it needs
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: essential amino acids cannot be made by the body, so they must come from dietary proteins.
A diet with no protein for a long time would therefore cause a shortage of essential amino acids. This matches option (1).
Option (2) is the tempting trap, but it reverses the facts. Non-essential amino acids can be made by the body itself.
Options (3) and (4) are wrong because the body can make some amino acids but not all of them.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Adenine
(B) Adenosine
(C) Adenylic acid
(D) Ribose
List-II:
(I) Nucleotide
(II) Pentose monosaccharide
(III) Purine base
(IV) Nucleoside
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Adenine is a purine base → III.
B. Adenosine is adenine + sugar, which is a nucleoside → IV.
C. Adenylic acid is a nucleoside + phosphate, which is a nucleotide → I.
D. Ribose is a pentose monosaccharide → II.
The common trap is mixing up adenosine (nucleoside) and adenylic acid (nucleotide).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: When a tissue is ground in trichloroacetic acid and strained, the polysaccharides are recovered in the acid-insoluble fraction.
Statement II: Inulin is a polymer of glucose, just like cellulose.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Grinding tissue in trichloroacetic acid separates small molecules into the acid-soluble filtrate. Macromolecules such as polysaccharides, proteins and nucleic acids stay in the acid-insoluble fraction.
Statement II is incorrect. Inulin is a polymer of fructose. Cellulose is a polymer of glucose.
So only Statement I is correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In biology, the primary structure of a protein refers to:
options: The folding of the polypeptide into a helix
The sequence of amino acids, that is, which amino acid is first, which is second, and so on
The arrangement of subunits with respect to each other
The three-dimensional folding of the chain like a ball
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: primary structure is the sequence of amino acids, i.e. which amino acid is first, second and so on.
It is the positional information of amino acids in the chain.
Why the others fail: helix folding is secondary structure, ball-like 3D folding is tertiary structure, and arrangement of subunits is quaternary structure.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about protein structure is incorrect?
options: Alpha helix and beta-pleated sheet are forms of secondary structure
The entire length of every protein thread is coiled into a right-handed helix
Quaternary structure is seen only in proteins made of more than one polypeptide or subunit
Tertiary structure gives a three-dimensional view of a protein
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet are forms of secondary structure.
(2) Incorrect: only some portions of a protein thread form a right-handed helix. Other regions fold into other forms, such as sheets.
(3) Correct: quaternary structure needs more than one polypeptide or subunit.
(4) Correct: tertiary structure gives the 3D view of a protein.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following biomolecules are homopolymers?
Cellulose, Insulin, Collagen, Inulin, Trypsin, Antibody
questions.explanation:
Cellulose is a homopolymer because it is made only of glucose units.
Inulin is a homopolymer because it is made only of fructose units.
Insulin, collagen, trypsin and antibodies are all proteins. Proteins are heteropolymers made of different amino acids, so none of these four count.
That gives two homopolymers, cellulose and inulin.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Secondary metabolites such as rubber, spices and scents are useful to human welfare.
Reason (R): The functions of all secondary metabolites in their host organisms are clearly known.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Rubber, drugs, spices, scents and pigments are all secondary metabolites that are useful to humans.
R is false. NCERT states that the roles or functions of all secondary metabolites in their host organisms are not yet understood.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Gingelly oil remains in liquid form even during winter.
Reason (R): Oils have a lower melting point than fats.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: gingelly (sesame) oil stays liquid in winter.
R is true: fats and oils differ by melting point, and oils have the lower melting point.
R explains A. Because the melting point of the oil is below winter temperatures, it does not solidify.
So both statements are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sugar present in the polynucleotide chain of DNA is:
questions.explanation:
A nucleic acid whose sugar is 2'-deoxyribose is deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).
Ribose is the sugar of RNA, which makes it the most tempting wrong option.
Glucose and fructose are hexoses and are not found in nucleic acids.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A homopolymer is best described as a polymer in which:
options: Only one type of monomer repeats n number of times
Twenty different types of monomers are joined together
Monomers are joined only by hydrogen bonds
Two polypeptide chains are joined together
questions.explanation:
Definition: a homopolymer is a polymer in which only one type of monomer repeats $n$ times. Cellulose, made only of glucose, is an example.
Option (2) describes a protein. Proteins are heteropolymers built from up to 20 different amino acids.
Option (3) is wrong because monomers in polymers are linked by covalent bonds, such as glycosidic or peptide bonds, not only by hydrogen bonds.
Option (4) describes a protein made of two polypeptide chains, which is a quaternary feature and not the definition of a homopolymer.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about enzymes and inorganic catalysts is INCORRECT?
options: Inorganic catalysts work efficiently at high temperatures and high pressures.
Enzymes of most organisms get damaged at high temperatures, say above 40°C.
Enzymes isolated from organisms of hot vents and sulphur springs remain stable up to about 80°-90°C.
Enzymes from thermophilic organisms lose their catalytic power at temperatures just above 40°C.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: inorganic catalysts work efficiently at high temperature and pressure.
(2) Correct: enzymes of most organisms are damaged above about 40°C.
(3) Correct: enzymes from organisms of hot vents and sulphur springs stay stable up to 80°-90°C.
(4) Incorrect: these thermophilic enzymes keep their catalytic power at 80°-90°C. Losing activity just above 40°C applies to ordinary enzymes, not thermophilic ones.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following about the reaction $CO_2 + H_2O \rightleftharpoons H_2CO_3$:
Statement I: In the absence of any enzyme, only about 200 molecules of $H_2CO_3$ are formed in an hour.
Statement II: Carbonic anhydrase, present in the cytoplasm, raises the rate to about 600,000 molecules per second, which is roughly a 10 million-fold acceleration.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Without an enzyme, only about 200 molecules of $H_2CO_3$ form per hour (NCERT).
Statement II is correct. Carbonic anhydrase, found in the cytoplasm, raises the rate to about 600,000 molecules per second.
Check: $6\times10^5 \times 3600 \approx 2.2\times10^9$ per hour. Dividing by 200 gives $\approx 10^7$, which is about a 10 million-fold acceleration.
So both statements are correct.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A potential energy versus progress-of-reaction graph shows substrate S at a higher energy level than product P. Two humps lie between them: a tall one labelled 'without enzyme' and a shorter one labelled 'with enzyme'. Which interpretation of this graph is correct?
options: Since P lies below S, the reaction needs no activation energy at all
The enzyme lowers the energy barrier to the transition state but does not change the energy difference between S and P
The enzyme makes the reaction exothermic by lowering the energy level of P
The transition state at the top of the hump is the most stable structure along the reaction pathway
questions.explanation:
The height of the hump above S is the activation energy. This is the energy needed to reach the transition state.
The enzyme gives a shorter hump, so it lowers the activation energy. The levels of S and P stay where they are, so the S–P energy difference does not change.
(1) is wrong: even an exothermic reaction has to pass through a transition state, so it still needs activation energy.
(3) is wrong: the enzyme does not change the energy of P.
(4) is wrong: the transition state is the least stable, highest-energy point on the pathway.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Thymidine and uridine both contain pyrimidine bases.
Statement II: In a nucleoside, a phosphate group is esterified to the sugar.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: thymine and uracil are pyrimidines, so their nucleosides thymidine and uridine contain pyrimidine bases.
Statement II is incorrect: a phosphate esterified to the sugar defines a nucleotide. A nucleoside is only base + sugar.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (discipline) with List-II (how 'structure' of a molecule is usually described).
List-I:
A. Inorganic chemistry
B. Organic chemistry
C. Physics
D. Biology (proteins)
List-II:
I. Three-dimensional view of molecules
II. Description at four levels
III. Molecular formula
IV. Two-dimensional view of molecules
questions.explanation:
A. Inorganic chemistry describes a molecule by its molecular formula, e.g. NaCl → III.
B. Organic chemistry draws a two-dimensional view, e.g. the benzene ring → IV.
C. Physics imagines a three-dimensional view of molecules → I.
D. Biology describes protein structure at four levels (primary to quaternary) → II.
So the matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Malonate decreases the activity of succinic dehydrogenase.
Reason (R): Malonate closely resembles succinate in structure and competes with it for the substrate-binding site of the enzyme.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: malonate lowers the activity of succinic dehydrogenase.
R is true: malonate is structurally similar to succinate, the substrate, and binds to the same substrate-binding site.
When malonate occupies that site, succinate cannot bind, so the enzyme works less. This is competitive inhibition.
R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are nucleosides?
Adenosine, Adenylic acid, Uridine, Guanine, Cytidine, Thymidylic acid, Thymidine
questions.explanation:
A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base joined to a pentose sugar, with no phosphate.
Nucleosides in the list: adenosine, uridine, cytidine and thymidine, which makes 4.
Adenylic acid and thymidylic acid carry a phosphate, so they are nucleotides.
Guanine is a free nitrogenous base.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Amino acids are grouped as acidic, basic or neutral based on the number of amino and carboxyl groups they carry. Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
questions.explanation:
A basic amino acid has an extra amino group in its R group.
Lysine has such an extra amino group, so it is basic.
Glutamic acid has an extra carboxyl group, so it is acidic.
Valine has one amino and one carboxyl group, so it is neutral.
Tyrosine carries a ring in its R group, so it is classed as aromatic.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A diagram shows a single long polypeptide chain folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball. Hydrogen bonds and disulphide bonds are labelled holding the folds together, and no other chain is present. This diagram represents which level of protein structure?
questions.explanation:
The diagram shows a single chain folded upon itself into a ball-like 3D shape. NCERT likens this to a hollow woollen ball, and it is tertiary structure.
Hydrogen and disulphide bonds stabilise these folds.
Why (4) fails: quaternary structure needs two or more subunits, but only one chain is present.
Secondary structure covers only local helices or sheets, and primary structure is just the amino acid sequence.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Cellulose does not give a blue colour when treated with iodine.
Reason (R): Cellulose does not contain complex helices and therefore cannot hold $I_2$ molecules.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: cellulose does not turn blue with iodine.
R is true: cellulose lacks complex helices, so it cannot hold $I_2$.
The blue colour of starch comes from $I_2$ held inside its helical regions.
Cellulose has no such helices, so it cannot bind iodine. R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following elements: H, C, O, N, S, Na, Ca, Mg, Si.
Using NCERT's Table 9.1, how many of these have a higher percentage by weight in the human body than in the earth's crust?
questions.explanation:
Compare body % with crust % for each element using Table 9.1.
Higher in the body: H (0.5 vs 0.14), C (18.5 vs 0.03), O (65.0 vs 46.6), N (3.3 vs very little), S (0.3 vs 0.03).
Higher in the crust: Na (0.2 vs 2.8), Ca (1.5 vs 3.6), Mg (0.1 vs 2.1), Si (negligible vs 27.7).
So 5 elements are more abundant in the human body.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A protein is a heteropolymer.
Reason (R): Only some portions of a protein thread are folded in the form of a helix.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: a protein is a heteropolymer because it is built from different kinds of amino acids (about 20 types).
R is true: only some portions of the protein thread form a helix, which is secondary structure.
R does not explain A. Partial helix formation describes folding, not the variety of monomers that makes a protein a heteropolymer.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: $\alpha$-amino acids are described as substituted methanes. The four groups that occupy the four valencies of the $\alpha$-carbon are:
options: Hydrogen, carboxyl group, amino group and R group
Hydrogen, hydroxyl group, amino group and R group
Two hydrogens, carboxyl group and amino group in all amino acids
Carboxyl group, amino group, phosphate group and R group
questions.explanation:
Amino acids are called substituted methanes because the four valencies of the $\alpha$-carbon carry four groups: H, a carboxyl group ($-COOH$), an amino group ($-NH_2$) and a variable R group.
Option (3) is tempting, but two hydrogens occur only in glycine, where R is itself H. It is not a general rule.
Options (2) and (4) wrongly include hydroxyl and phosphate groups.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: All the elements present in a sample of earth's crust are also present in a sample of living tissue.
Statement II: Sodium, calcium and magnesium have a higher percentage by weight in the human body than in the earth's crust.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that all elements found in a sample of earth's crust are also found in living tissue. The lists match qualitatively; only the relative amounts differ.
Statement II is incorrect. All three are more abundant in the crust:
- Na: 2.8 (crust) vs 0.2 (body)
- Ca: 3.6 vs 1.5
- Mg: 2.1 vs 0.1
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following pairs do BOTH compounds belong to the same category of secondary metabolites as given in NCERT?
questions.explanation:
NCERT's table of secondary metabolites puts each compound in one category.
(1) Mixed: ricin is a toxin, but concanavalin A is a lectin.
(2) Mixed: codeine is an alkaloid, but curcumin is a drug.
(3) Same: carotenoids and anthocyanins are both pigments.
(4) Mixed: rubber is a polymeric substance, but lemon grass oil is an essential oil.
Only pair (3) shares one category.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Three proteinaceous amino acids, X, Y and Z, differ only in their R groups:
X: the R group carries an additional carboxyl group
Y: the R group carries an additional amino group
Z: the R group is a methyl group
Based on the number of amino and carboxyl groups, X, Y and Z would respectively be classified as:
questions.explanation:
X: The R group adds a second carboxyl group, so there are more –COOH than –NH$_2$ groups. X is acidic (e.g., glutamic acid).
Y: The R group adds a second amino group, so Y is basic (e.g., lysine).
Z: A methyl R group gives alanine. Alanine has one amino and one carboxyl group, so it is neutral.
Z has no ring in its R group, so it is not aromatic. This rules out options (1) and (4).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Malonate acts as a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase because its structure closely resembles that of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase.
Statement II: Once all enzyme molecules are saturated with substrate, further increase in substrate concentration does not raise the reaction velocity beyond $V_{max}$.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Malonate is a competitive inhibitor because it resembles the substrate succinate, not the enzyme. This lets it compete for the substrate-binding site.
Statement II is correct. Enzyme molecules are far fewer than substrate molecules. Once all of them are occupied, adding more substrate cannot raise velocity, so it plateaus at $V_{max}$.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The rate of a process is defined as $\frac{\delta P}{\delta t}$. According to the general rule of thumb, how does this rate change when the temperature is raised by 10°C?
questions.explanation:
Rate $= \delta P/\delta t$, the amount of product formed per unit time.
NCERT rule of thumb: the rate doubles for every 10°C rise in temperature and halves for every 10°C fall.
So a 10°C rise roughly doubles the rate.
The tenfold option is a trap. It mistakes the size of the temperature step (10°C) for the size of the change in rate.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student weighs a fresh leaf, dries it completely and weighs it again. The student then burns the dried material fully. Which of the following statements about this analysis is INCORRECT?
options: The difference between the wet weight and the dry weight mainly represents the water content of the leaf.
On complete burning, the carbon compounds are oxidised to $CO_2$ and water vapour, which escape.
The ash left behind contains inorganic elements such as calcium and magnesium.
Inorganic compounds such as sulphate and phosphate appear in the acid-insoluble fraction, not in the acid-soluble fraction.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: drying removes water, so wet weight minus dry weight is mainly the water content.
(2) Correct: on complete burning, carbon compounds are oxidised to $CO_2$ and water vapour, and both escape as gases.
(3) Correct: the ash left behind holds inorganic elements such as Ca and Mg.
(4) Incorrect: NCERT places inorganic compounds such as $SO_4^{2-}$ and $PO_4^{3-}$ in the acid-soluble fraction. The acid-insoluble fraction holds macromolecules: proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and membrane lipids.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following elements:
Hydrogen, Carbon, Oxygen, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Silicon, Sulphur
How many of these have a higher percentage by weight in the earth's crust than in the human body?
questions.explanation: Four elements are more abundant in the crust: sodium (2.8 vs 0.2), calcium (3.6 vs 1.5), magnesium (2.1 vs 0.1) and silicon (27.7 vs negligible). Hydrogen, carbon, oxygen and sulphur are all higher in the human body. Oxygen is the trap: although it is about 46.6% of the crust, it makes up 65% of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Palmitic acid, a common fatty acid, contains how many carbon atoms in total, including the carboxyl carbon?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that palmitic acid has 16 carbons, including the carboxyl carbon.
Arachidonic acid has 20 carbons, which makes option (4) the tempting trap.
The 14-carbon option matches myristic acid, and the 18-carbon option matches stearic acid.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (amino acid) with List-II (category).
List-I:
(A) Glutamic acid
(B) Lysine
(C) Valine
(D) Tryptophan
List-II:
(I) Neutral
(II) Aromatic
(III) Acidic
(IV) Basic
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Glutamic acid has an extra –COOH group, so it is acidic → III.
(B) Lysine has an extra –NH$_2$ group, so it is basic → IV.
(C) Valine has one amino and one carboxyl group, so it is neutral → I.
(D) Tryptophan has a ring structure in its R group, so it is aromatic → II.
The matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The most abundant component of living organisms is
questions.explanation:
Water is the most abundant chemical in living organisms, making up about 70–90% of total cellular mass.
Proteins are the most abundant organic compound, which is why option (1) is tempting. However, they form only about 10–15% of cell mass.
Sugars and nucleic acids form even smaller fractions.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 9 (MCQ Q8)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.
Statement II: Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO) is the most abundant protein in the whole of the biosphere.
Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world only, not in the whole biosphere.
Statement II is correct. RuBisCO, the $CO_2$-fixing enzyme of photosynthesis, is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Beyond a certain point, increasing the substrate concentration does not raise the velocity of an enzyme-catalysed reaction above $V_{max}$.
Reason (R): The enzyme molecules are fewer than the substrate molecules, and once they are saturated no free enzyme is left to bind the extra substrate.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. At high [S], velocity plateaus at $V_{max}$ and does not exceed it.
R is true. Enzyme molecules are fewer than substrate molecules. Once all enzyme molecules are saturated, no free enzyme is left to bind extra substrate.
Saturation stops further ES complex formation. This is exactly why velocity stops rising, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The acid-soluble pool represents roughly the cytoplasmic composition of a cell.
Statement II: Like polysaccharides, lipids have molecular weights of ten thousand daltons and above.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The acid-soluble pool (filtrate) roughly represents the cytoplasmic composition of the cell.
Statement II is incorrect. Polysaccharides are polymers of ≥10,000 Da, but lipids are small molecules of molecular weight not exceeding about 800 Da. Lipids are the exception in the acid-insoluble fraction.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are secondary metabolites?
Morphine, Concanavalin A, Glycine, Ricin, Carotenoids, Lecithin, Curcumin, Vinblastin
questions.explanation:
Secondary metabolites are compounds whose role in the host is not well understood, unlike primary metabolites.
The secondary metabolites here are:
- morphine (alkaloid)
- concanavalin A (lectin)
- ricin (toxin)
- carotenoids (pigment)
- curcumin and vinblastin (drugs)
That makes 6.
Glycine is an amino acid and lecithin is a phospholipid. Both have known physiological roles, so they are primary metabolites.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An amino acid is dissolved in water and the pH is then varied. Which of the following correctly describes its zwitterionic form?
options: $^{+}H_3N-CH(R)-COO^{-}$, carrying both a positive and a negative charge with no net charge
questions.explanation:
A zwitterion carries a positive and a negative charge on the same molecule, so its net charge is zero.
In this form the amino group is protonated ($-NH_3^+$) and the carboxyl group is ionised ($-COO^-$). This gives $^{+}H_3N-CH(R)-COO^{-}$.
Option (2) is the cationic form, which predominates at low (acidic) pH.
Option (4) is the anionic form, which predominates at high (basic) pH.
Option (1) shows no ionisation at all, so it is not a zwitterion.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When iodine solution is added to a sample, a blue colour develops. Which polysaccharide is most likely present?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: starch forms helical secondary structures that can hold $I_2$ molecules. The starch–iodine complex is blue.
So a blue colour with iodine shows that starch is present.
Cellulose has no complex helices, so it cannot hold iodine and gives no blue colour.
Chitin and inulin do not give this test either.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: The acid-insoluble fraction contains only four types of organic compounds.
Biomolecules with molecular weights below one thousand daltons are called micromolecules.
Lipids, together with polysaccharides, polypeptides and nucleic acids, form the true macromolecular fraction of a cell.
Carbohydrates and lipids together account for roughly 5% of the total cellular mass.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. The acid-insoluble fraction has only four types of organic compounds: proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids.
(2) Correct. Biomolecules below 1000 Da are called micromolecules.
(3) Incorrect. Only polysaccharides, polypeptides and nucleic acids are true macromolecules. Lipids (≤800 Da) are not strictly macromolecules.
(4) Correct. Carbohydrates (3%) plus lipids (2%) give about 5% of cellular mass.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: A protein consisting of only a single polypeptide chain cannot have a quaternary structure.
Statement II: If the order of amino acids in a polypeptide is changed without changing which amino acids are present or how many, its primary structure changes.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Quaternary structure is the arrangement of two or more polypeptide subunits, so a protein with a single chain cannot have it.
Statement II is correct. Primary structure is the sequence, i.e. the positional order of amino acids. Rearranging the same amino acids therefore changes the primary structure, even though the composition stays the same.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are nucleotides?
Adenosine, guanylic acid, thymidine, cytidylic acid, uracil, uridylic acid
questions.explanation:
Nucleotides carry a phosphate esterified to the sugar; names ending in '-ylic acid' are nucleotides.
Nucleotides: guanylic acid, cytidylic acid and uridylic acid.
Nucleosides: adenosine and thymidine (base + sugar, no phosphate).
Free base: uracil.
So there are 3 nucleotides.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A nitrogenous base attached to a sugar, without any phosphate group, is called a nucleoside. Which of the following is a nucleoside?
questions.explanation:
A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base joined to a sugar, with no phosphate.
Uridine is uracil + ribose, so it is a nucleoside.
Uridylic acid also carries a phosphate ester, so it is a nucleotide; this is the tempting wrong choice.
Uracil is only a base, and ribose is only a sugar.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about co-factors are correct?
(i) Prosthetic groups are organic compounds tightly bound to the apoenzyme.
(ii) Haem is the prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase.
(iii) Co-enzymes remain permanently bound to the apoenzyme, even when no catalysis is occurring.
(iv) NAD and NADP contain the vitamin niacin.
(v) Zinc is a metal ion co-factor for carboxypeptidase.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: prosthetic groups are organic and tightly bound to the apoenzyme.
(ii) Correct: haem is the prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase.
(iii) Incorrect: co-enzymes bind the apoenzyme only transiently, usually during catalysis. Tight binding is the feature of prosthetic groups.
(iv) Correct: NAD and NADP contain niacin.
(v) Correct: zinc is the metal ion co-factor of carboxypeptidase.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a protein molecule, the amino acids are joined to one another in a linear chain by which type of bond?
questions.explanation:
Proteins are polypeptides, which are linear chains of amino acids.
Each peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next, with loss of water.
The other bonds belong to different biomolecules:
- Glycosidic bonds join monosaccharides in polysaccharides.
- Phosphodiester bonds join nucleotides in nucleic acids.
- Ester bonds join fatty acids to glycerol in lipids.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Enzymes are divided into 6 classes, each with 4–13 subclasses, and are named by a four-digit number.
Statement II: Enzymes that catalyse hydrolysis of peptide and glycosidic bonds are placed in the class lyases.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Enzymes fall into 6 classes, each with 4–13 subclasses, and each enzyme is named by a four-digit number.
Statement II is incorrect. Hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide and glycosidic bonds is catalysed by hydrolases.
Lyases instead remove groups by non-hydrolytic mechanisms, leaving double bonds.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The following events of an enzyme's catalytic cycle are given in jumbled order:
P. The active site breaks chemical bonds of the substrate and an enzyme-product complex forms
Q. The substrate binds to and fits into the active site
R. The free enzyme releases the products and is ready for another substrate molecule
S. Substrate binding induces the enzyme to alter its shape and fit more tightly around the substrate
Choose the correct sequence:
questions.explanation:
The catalytic cycle follows $E + S \rightarrow ES \rightarrow EP \rightarrow E + P$.
Q: First, the substrate binds to the active site.
S: Binding induces the enzyme to change shape and fit more tightly around the substrate (induced fit). This must come after binding, which rules out option (3).
P: The active site breaks the substrate's bonds, forming the enzyme–product complex.
R: The products are released, and the free enzyme is ready for another substrate molecule. Release must come last, which rules out option (4).
So the order is Q, S, P, R.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Palmitic acid
B. Arachidonic acid
C. Lecithin
D. Gingelly oil
List-II
I. Phospholipid found in cell membranes
II. 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon
III. Glyceride with low melting point that stays liquid in winter
IV. 16 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. Palmitic acid has 16 carbons, counting the carboxyl carbon → IV.
B. Arachidonic acid has 20 carbons, counting the carboxyl carbon → II.
C. Lecithin is a phospholipid found in cell membranes → I.
D. Gingelly oil has a low melting point, so it stays liquid in winter → III.
The tempting trap is swapping 16 and 20 between the two fatty acids, as options (2) and (4) do.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about lipids are correct?
(i) In a fatty acid, the R group attached to the carboxyl group may contain 1 to 19 carbon atoms.
(ii) In palmitic acid, $CH_3(CH_2)_{14}COOH$, the R group contains 15 carbon atoms.
(iii) A triglyceride has three fatty acid molecules esterified to one glycerol molecule.
(iv) Lipids are true macromolecules, which is why they separate into the acid-insoluble fraction.
(v) Unsaturated fatty acids are those that lack C=C double bonds.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the R group may be methyl, ethyl or a longer chain of $CH_2$ groups, with 1 to 19 carbons.
(ii) Correct: 1 $CH_3$ + 14 $CH_2$ = 15 carbons in R. Adding the carboxyl carbon gives 16 in total.
(iii) Correct: a triglyceride is glycerol esterified with three fatty acids.
(iv) Incorrect: lipids are small molecules (below 800 Da). They appear in the acid-insoluble fraction only because they form membrane vesicles.
(v) Incorrect: unsaturated fatty acids contain one or more C=C bonds.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the amino acid serine, the variable R group attached to the $\alpha$-carbon is:
questions.explanation:
Every amino acid has an $\alpha$-carbon bearing H, $-COOH$, $-NH_2$ and a variable R group.
In serine, the R group is hydroxymethyl, $-CH_2OH$.
A hydrogen atom as R gives glycine, and a methyl group as R gives alanine. These are the usual mix-ups.
An aromatic ring is seen in phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan, not in serine.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is an aromatic amino acid?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists tyrosine, phenylalanine and tryptophan as the aromatic amino acids.
Tryptophan has an aromatic indole ring in its R group, so it fits.
The other options belong to different classes:
- Valine is neutral.
- Lysine is basic.
- Glutamic acid is acidic.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Morphine and codeine are secondary metabolites. In which category of secondary metabolites are they placed?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives morphine and codeine as examples of alkaloids.
The other categories have different examples: terpenoids are monoterpenes and diterpenes, the lectin is concanavalin A, and the toxins are abrin and ricin.
Toxins can be a tempting choice because morphine and codeine act strongly on the body. NCERT still classifies them as alkaloids, not toxins.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Amino acid)
A. Glutamic acid
B. Lysine
C. Valine
D. Phenylalanine
List-II (Category)
I. Neutral
II. Aromatic
III. Acidic
IV. Basic
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. Glutamic acid has an extra carboxyl group, so it is acidic (III).
B. Lysine has an extra amino group, so it is basic (IV).
C. Valine is neutral (I).
D. Phenylalanine has a benzene ring, so it is aromatic (II).
Swapping glutamic acid and lysine gives option (2), which is a common error.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about nucleic acids is incorrect?
options: A nucleotide consists of a heterocyclic nitrogen base, a monosaccharide and a phosphate
Uracil is a substituted purine found in RNA
The nucleic acid containing 2' deoxyribose is called DNA
Adenine and guanine are substituted purines
questions.explanation:
Statement (1) is correct: a nucleotide contains a heterocyclic base, a sugar and a phosphate.
Statement (2) is incorrect: uracil is a substituted pyrimidine, like cytosine and thymine, not a purine.
Statement (3) is correct: the nucleic acid containing 2' deoxyribose is DNA.
Statement (4) is correct: adenine and guanine are substituted purines.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (level of protein structure) with List-II (description) and choose the correct option.
List-I
A. Primary structure
B. Secondary structure
C. Tertiary structure
D. Quaternary structure
List-II
(i) Arrangement of individual folded polypeptides or subunits with respect to one another
(ii) Positional information, that is, which amino acid comes first, second and so on
(iii) The long chain folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball
(iv) Some portions of the thread folded like a revolving staircase
questions.explanation:
A. Primary structure is the sequence of amino acids, i.e. which comes first, second and so on → (ii).
B. Secondary structure is local folding such as the right-handed helix, which looks like a revolving staircase → (iv).
C. Tertiary structure is the whole chain folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball → (iii).
D. Quaternary structure is the arrangement of separate folded polypeptides or subunits relative to each other → (i).
Option (2) swaps the staircase and woollen-ball descriptions, which is the usual trap.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Inulin is a polysaccharide made of fructose units.
Statement II: In a glycogen chain, the right end is called the non-reducing end and the left end is called the reducing end.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: inulin is a polymer of fructose.
Statement II is incorrect: in a polysaccharide chain such as glycogen, the right end is the reducing end and the left end is the non-reducing end. The statement swaps the two ends.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Enzymes are biocatalysts. They catalyse biochemical reactions. In general they reduce activation energy of reactions. Many physico-chemical processes are enzyme mediated. Which of the following reactions is not enzyme-mediated in biological system?
options: Untwining the two strands of DNA
questions.explanation:
(1) Dissolving $CO_2$ in water is a simple physical process. It needs no enzyme.
(2) Separating (unwinding) the two DNA strands is done by the enzyme helicase.
(3) Sucrose is hydrolysed to glucose and fructose by invertase (sucrase).
(4) Peptide bonds are formed by peptidyl transferase during translation.
Only the dissolving of $CO_2$ is not enzyme-mediated.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 9 (MCQ Q14)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A nucleotide is built from three chemically distinct components. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation:
A nucleotide has three components: a heterocyclic nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) and a phosphate.
Glycerol is not one of them. It is the backbone of glycerides and phospholipids.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Adult human haemoglobin is made up of:
options: Two subunits, one of $\alpha$ type and one of $\beta$ type
Four subunits: three of $\alpha$ type and one of $\beta$ type
Four subunits: two of $\alpha$ type and two of $\beta$ type
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): adult human haemoglobin has 4 subunits. Two are of the $\alpha$ type and two are of the $\beta$ type.
So the subunits are identical only in pairs, which matches option (4).
Why the others fail: (1) gives only two subunits. (2) makes all four identical. (3) has the wrong ratio of $\alpha$ to $\beta$.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (enzyme class) with List-II (type of reaction catalysed):
List-I
A. Transferases
B. Lyases
C. Isomerases
D. Ligases
List-II
I. Inter-conversion of optical, geometric or positional isomers
II. Linking together of two compounds, e.g., forming C–N or P–O bonds
III. Transfer of a group other than hydrogen between a pair of substrates
IV. Removal of groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. Transferases transfer a group G (other than hydrogen) from S to S'. So A-III.
B. Lyases remove groups by non-hydrolytic means and leave double bonds. So B-IV.
C. Isomerases interconvert optical, geometric or positional isomers. So C-I.
D. Ligases link two compounds by forming bonds such as C–N or P–O. So D-II.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Adenine and guanine are substituted purines, whereas cytosine, uracil and thymine are substituted pyrimidines.
Removing the phosphate group from adenylic acid would leave adenosine.
Lipids, polysaccharides and nucleic acids together constitute the true macromolecular fraction of a cell.
DNA and RNA both consist of nucleotides only and function as genetic material.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: A and G are substituted purines; C, U and T are substituted pyrimidines.
(2) Correct: adenylic acid minus phosphate is adenosine, the nucleoside.
(3) Incorrect: the true macromolecules are polysaccharides, proteins and nucleic acids. Lipids (MW < 800 Da) enter the acid-insoluble fraction only because membrane fragments form vesicles.
(4) Correct per NCERT: DNA and RNA consist of nucleotides only and act as genetic material.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Enzymes isolated from organisms living in hot vents and sulphur springs can retain catalytic activity at 80°–90°C.
Reason (R): Low temperature permanently destroys enzyme activity by denaturing the protein.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: enzymes from thermophilic organisms in hot vents and sulphur springs are thermostable and stay active at 80°–90°C.
R is false: low temperature only keeps an enzyme temporarily inactive, and activity returns on warming. It is high temperature that denatures the protein and destroys activity.
A is true and R is false.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following amino acids are aromatic?
Tyrosine, Valine, Phenylalanine, Serine, Tryptophan, Alanine, Lysine, Glycine
questions.explanation:
Aromatic amino acids: tyrosine, phenylalanine and tryptophan. That makes 3.
Non-aromatic amino acids in the list:
- Valine and alanine are neutral.
- Serine has a $-CH_2OH$ group.
- Lysine is basic.
- Glycine has H as its R group.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A biomolecule is made of the nitrogen base uracil attached to a ribose sugar, with no phosphate group. This molecule is best described as a:
questions.explanation:
A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base attached to a sugar, with no phosphate.
Uracil + ribose is therefore a nucleoside, uridine.
It is not a nucleotide, which would need a phosphate esterified to the sugar (uridylic acid).
It is not a free base or a polynucleotide either.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (enzyme class) with List-II (type of reaction catalysed):
List-I
A. Oxidoreductases
B. Transferases
C. Lyases
D. Ligases
List-II
(i) Joining two compounds, forming C–O, C–S, C–N or P–O bonds
(ii) Removal of groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis, leaving double bonds
(iii) Transfer of a group other than hydrogen between a pair of substrates
(iv) Oxidoreduction between two substrates S and S'
questions.explanation:
A. Oxidoreductases catalyse oxidoreduction between substrates S and S': (iv).
B. Transferases transfer a group other than hydrogen between substrates: (iii).
C. Lyases remove groups without hydrolysis, leaving double bonds: (ii).
D. Ligases join two compounds, forming C–O, C–S, C–N or P–O bonds: (i).
The usual trap is swapping lyases (removal) with ligases (joining).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Palmitic acid
(B) Arachidonic acid
(C) Glycerol
(D) Lecithin
List-II
(I) Phospholipid
(II) 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon
(III) Trihydroxy propane
(IV) 16 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon
questions.explanation:
A–IV: palmitic acid has 16 carbons, including the carboxyl carbon.
B–II: arachidonic acid has 20 carbons, including the carboxyl carbon.
C–III: glycerol is trihydroxy propane.
D–I: lecithin is a phospholipid.
The common trap is swapping the 16 and 20 carbon counts, which gives option (2).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which chemical makes up the largest share of the total mass of a cell?
questions.explanation:
Water makes up 70-90% of total cellular mass, so it is the most abundant chemical in living cells.
Proteins come next at 10-15%. Nucleic acids are 5-7%, carbohydrates about 3%, lipids about 2% and ions about 1%.
Proteins are the most abundant organic compound, but water is far greater by total mass.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase needs which cofactor for its activity?
questions.explanation:
Some enzymes need a non-protein cofactor to work. NCERT names three kinds: prosthetic groups, coenzymes and metal ions.
Carboxypeptidase is NCERT's example of an enzyme that needs a metal ion. Zinc ($Zn^{2+}$) forms coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and with the substrate.
Haem is wrong because it is the prosthetic group of peroxidase and catalase.
NAD is a coenzyme for dehydrogenases, and niacin is the vitamin inside NAD. Niacin is not a prosthetic group of carboxypeptidase.
Answer: (2)
